spans.assertion: position was adjusted for because different positions carry different disciplinary risk, and dark-skinned players are overrepresented in forward positions and underrepresented as goalkeepers
league country was adjusted for because disciplinary standards vary across leagues, and dark-skinned players are more common in England and France than Germany and Spain
games (exposure) was adjusted for because more games create more opportunities for red cards

the adjusted risk difference was computed via marginal standardization: fitting the logistic model, generating predicted probabilities under counterfactual all-light and all-dark scenarios, taking the mean difference, and converting to percentage points
the 95% confidence interval was calculated using the delta method with a parametric bootstrap of 5,000 draws from the asymptotic multivariate normal distribution of parameter estimates
the p-value came from a two-sided test using the Z-statistic from the delta-method standard error

the analysis treated player-referee dyads as independent observations

player-referee dyads are not fully independent because the same player appears with multiple referees and the same referee with multiple players, inducing clustering and potential correlation in outcomes
the delta-method approach used for the confidence interval did not explicitly model within-player or within-referee correlation (clustering), which may mean standard errors are underestimated

a more conservative approach using cluster-robust standard errors or mixed-effects models with random intercepts for players/referees would have been preferable, which could widen confidence intervals and increase p-values, but was not used

despite adjusting for position, residual within-position confounding (e.g., dark-skinned center forwards playing an unmeasured more aggressive style) is considered possible, but the continuous skin-tone specification's stronger effect and the consistency of results across sensitivity analyses are interpreted as arguing against substantial residual confounding
games is described as a crude/imperfect measure of exposure, potentially leaving residual confounding to the extent it imperfectly captures exposure
minutes played would have been preferred as the exposure measure, but was not available at the dyad level
country-level implicit and explicit bias measures (IAT scores, racial thermometer) were available in the dataset but were not included in the primary model
including the country-level bias measures did not substantively change results, though this check was not shown
individual referee-level bias measures would have been preferable to the country-level aggregates that were used
